diagram_math_checks.evidence: Coordinates give a convex octagon with distinct vertices v0,...,v7 in that cyclic order. Its eight explicit boundary segments read a,b,a^{-1},b^{-1},c,d,c^{-1},d^{-1}, exactly the Given data and Example. All eight edges including v7-v0 visibly render; no --cycle path is used.

The a arrows are v0->v1 and v3->v2, giving v0~v3,v1~v2. The b arrows are v1->v2 and v4->v3, giving v1~v4,v2~v3. The c arrows are v4->v5 and v7->v6, giving v4~v7,v5~v6. The d arrows are v5->v6 and v0->v7, giving v5~v0,v6~v7. These are exactly step 1.1. Inverse labels record cyclic traversal rather than arrow direction, explicitly explained in the caption; pairing is affine in the matching reference directions and reverses boundary traversal.

The dashed straight segment joins v0 to v4, lies otherwise strictly inside the convex octagon, and separates the left pentagon v0,v1,v2,v3,v4 (P1) from the right pentagon v4,v5,v6,v7,v0 (P2), exactly step 1.2. It is not an extra paired edge of the original schema.

The caption q:P->Y=P/R has polygon domain and quotient codomain. The eight endpoint identifications just checked generate one corner class (step 1.1); four side pairs give E=4 and the original disk interior F=1. The identification Y congruent to T^2#T^2 is the existing step 3.1 conclusion, not inferred from the picture. No new defining clause or dependency is introduced.
The existing Verification is byte-preserved. Its cut/gluing argument and count computation remain independent of the added illustration.
